market_mood: Risk is coming off the AI trade ahead of Nvidia's first earnings without Jensen Huang, while oil slides to $87 on a projected fourth-quarter surplus even as Iran-Gulf violence escalates. Deal news is heavy (Quebecor-Telus, Diamondback, Canadian Natural) and a KC Fed official says the Fed still 'has work to do on inflation.'
self_check: My high-confidence calls have been badly wrong (2 of 14) while low-confidence ones work best, so today's book is all medium and low; oil-themed calls have been my worst recent theme (1 of 8 in two weeks), so I avoided direct energy longs and used oil only as a cost tailwind for airlines.

picks.reason: The Kansas City Fed chief says the Fed 'has some work to do on inflation,' and the dollar keeps rallying — both point to long-term yields staying high, which pushes long bond prices down.

Iran struck Bahrain, Houthis fired missiles at Riyadh and mines hit tankers in Hormuz; sustained Gulf conflict supports missile-defense and munitions demand, and GD is less crowded than the big missile names.
A C$31B Quebecor bid for Telus re-rates the whole Canadian telecom group.
Rising truck and ocean shipping costs push freight toward cheaper rail.
A projected Q4 crude surplus undercuts the energy sector's recent outperformance.

Holding up better than tech, helped by energy and staples strength over the past week.
No major company news; mentioned only in a piece about mega-cap concentration in index funds.
Microsoft explained the glitch behind the worldwide Outlook outage; minor reputational noise, no financial impact flagged.
Earnings this week under interim CEO Colette Kress, with Trump floating Huang's possible return and shareholder litigation pending — unusually high event risk.
AWS signed a $5B data center deal with a Blackstone vehicle, underlining continued heavy cloud capacity spending.
Commentary says search query volumes are rebounding; the open question is whether that converts into ad revenue.
A $4.1B fund exited its entire Meta stake last quarter; no fundamental news today.
Prediction-market odds of a Tesla-SpaceX merger by April 2027 jumped above 60%, and Cybercab sales start with invited customers — speculative, headline-driven moves.
Its survey says GLP-1 out-of-pocket costs may need to halve to unlock growth; no bank-specific news.
Started production at Uaru in Guyana, lifting capacity to 1.1 million bpd, but crude slipping to $87 caps the upside.

Hawkish Fed commentary on unfinished inflation work and a rallying dollar argue for higher long yields and lower bond prices.

top_buys.pitch: Hawkish Fed commentary and a strong dollar keep pressure on long bond prices.
top_buys.why: The Kansas City Fed president said the Fed still 'has some work to do on inflation,' which pushes back on expectations of quick rate cuts. The dollar is extending a rally and global rate paths are in focus, both consistent with higher long-term yields. TLT falls when those yields rise, and this same trade worked for me a week ago.
top_buys.risks: A sharp equity selloff or soft inflation data could send money into Treasuries and lift TLT instead.
top_buys.watch: Upcoming inflation prints and further Fed speakers before the December meeting.

top_buys.pitch: Gulf conflict keeps widening, and General Dynamics is a less-crowded way to play munitions and defense demand.
top_buys.why: Iran attacked Bahrain and a US base, Houthis fired ballistic missiles at Riyadh, and mines struck three tankers in Hormuz — a sustained escalation, not a one-day scare. Rising demand for air and missile defense, munitions and anti-jamming gear supports multi-year defense budgets. GD also has a steady combat systems and Gulfstream business that cushions the stock.
top_buys.risks: A US-Iran deal or de-escalation would quickly deflate defense premiums, and industrials were weak last week.
top_buys.watch: Any US-Iran negotiation headlines and new Gulf defense orders.

top_buys.pitch: A C$31B Quebecor bid for Telus re-rates the whole Canadian telecom group.
top_buys.why: Quebecor's offer for Telus puts a concrete takeout valuation on Canadian wireless assets, and Telus jumped 9.5%. Peers like Rogers often follow as investors reassess sector values and consider consolidation knock-ons. Rogers hasn't moved the way Telus has, so the second-order effect may still unfold.
top_buys.risks: Canadian regulators are hostile to telecom consolidation, and the bid could collapse, taking sector enthusiasm with it.
top_buys.watch: Telus board response and any comment from Canadian competition authorities.

top_buys.pitch: Rising truck and ocean shipping costs push freight toward cheaper rail.
top_buys.why: Transportation executives say shipping costs are rising and retailers are being cautious with holiday inventory. Rail is the lower-cost option when trucking and ocean rates climb, and lower diesel prices from the oil decline help margins. Industrials sold off last week, so the entry is less crowded.
top_buys.risks: Weak retail volumes would hurt rail carloads regardless of cost advantages.
top_buys.watch: Weekly rail carload data and holiday retail sales updates.

top_buys.pitch: A projected Q4 crude surplus undercuts the energy sector's recent outperformance.
top_buys.why: Oil fell to $87 as Middle East exports recover and forecasters see supply exceeding demand this quarter. Energy was the best sector last week, up 3.3%, largely on war-risk premium that is now deflating. Majors with heavy upstream exposure give back the most when that premium fades.
top_buys.risks: Any new Hormuz incident or tanker attack would spike crude and this trade immediately.
top_buys.watch: OPEC and IEA supply updates, plus Hormuz shipping headlines.

summary.big_story: Oil slid to $87 on surplus forecasts even as Iran-Gulf attacks escalate, while the AI trade wobbles ahead of Nvidia's first earnings without Jensen Huang.
summary.top_pick: Short long-dated Treasuries via TLT, since hawkish Fed talk on inflation plus a rallying dollar should keep long yields elevated.
summary.watch: Nvidia's earnings and any confirmation on Huang's return, plus whether crude keeps falling through $87.
